questions.stem: What is the smallest particle of an element that retains the chemical properties of that element?
questions.explanation: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that retains the chemical properties of that element. Atoms are about 0.1 to 0.5 nanometres in diameter.

questions.stem: What determines which element an atom belongs to?

options.text: The total mass of the atom

questions.explanation: The number of protons in the nucleus defines which element an atom is. All atoms of the same element have the same number of protons.

questions.stem: Which part of the atom contains almost all of its mass?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons and holds almost all of the atom's mass. It is very small compared to the overall size of the atom.

questions.stem: The chemical symbol for sodium is Na, which comes from the Latin word 'Natrium'. What is the chemical symbol for iron?
questions.explanation: The chemical symbol for iron is Fe, derived from the Latin word 'Ferrum'. Many element symbols come from their Latin names rather than their English names.

questions.stem: A student writes 'CO' when they mean to refer to the element cobalt. Why is this incorrect?

options.text: CO represents carbon monoxide, a compound; cobalt is written as Co
The symbol for cobalt should be written as co
There is no difference between CO and Co

questions.explanation: CO (both letters capitalised) represents the compound carbon monoxide. The element cobalt is written as Co, with only the first letter capitalised. Correct capitalisation in chemical symbols is essential.

questions.stem: How are elements arranged in the Periodic Table?

options.text: In alphabetical order of their names
In order of increasing atomic mass only
In order of increasing atomic number, with similar properties in vertical columns
Randomly, grouped only by physical state

questions.explanation: Elements in the Periodic Table are arranged by increasing atomic number (number of protons). Elements with similar properties appear in vertical columns called groups.

questions.stem: Which statement about atoms in chemical reactions is correct?

options.text: Atoms can be created during chemical reactions
Atoms can be destroyed during chemical reactions
Atoms cannot be created, destroyed, or divided in chemical reactions
Atoms are split into smaller particles in chemical reactions

questions.explanation: Atoms cannot be created, destroyed, or divided in chemical reactions. They are rearranged to form new substances, but the atoms themselves remain unchanged.
